title: Adaptive SLO escalation and signal pruning — post-incident action items
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Follow-up from the 2026-03-08 capacity/regression incident where sustained KV-cache pressure and an unexpected scheduling regression caused repeated short-duration SLO breaches and a high volume of transient alerts. The immediate incident was contained by fallbacks but the alert stream generated >120 noisy notifications across oncall rotations, increasing time-to-resolution and creating paging fatigue. This ticket bundles the cross-team action items to reduce noisy SLO alerts while preserving fast detection of true degradations.

Findings: 1) Our current SLO breach alerts fire on 1-minute burn-rate windows and don't differentiate transient spikes from sustained burns; 2) Deployment/tag metadata is not propagated to many downstream alert rules, causing release-induced noise to be paged; 3) There is no intermediate escalation stage between page and dashboard-only for low-impact, self-healing breaches; 4) Some rate-limit and capacity alerts are conflated with SLO breach alerts, increasing ambiguity for responders.

Primary goals: - Reduce paging noise by introducing a two-stage escalator for SLO breaches (detect->verify->page) with an automated short suppression for self-resolving bursts. - Prune noisy signals by separating short-lived spikes (informational) from sustained regressions (paging). - Ensure deployment windows and planned maintenance can be automatically annotated to suppress non-actionable alerts.

Artifacts: Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/SLO-Incident-2026-03-08; Runtime PR with metric tagging changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4213; Proposal design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XampleLinkForSLODesign
acceptance_criteria: New SLO alert policy implemented that requires a 3-minute confirmation window before paging for the primary SLO metric (or an explicit fast-path for critical customer-facing endpoints)
Dashboard-only (no-page) tier created for transient SLO violations with automatic escalation if the violation persists beyond the confirmation window
Deployment/maintenance tags are propagated to alert evaluation and used to automatically mute non-critical alerts during rollout windows
Oncall page volume for SLO alerts reduced by >=60% in the first 30 days post-deploy (measured by alert count and unique pages)
Runbooks updated with clear decision criteria and an automated playbook that responders can trigger to immediately silence replicated transient alerts
follow_up_tasks: ENG-12757: Implement 3-minute confirmation window and a rolling-average check to distinguish 1-min spikes from sustained burns — owner: Dylan Chen — due: 2026-03-18
ENG-12758: Add deployment tag propagation in the runtime and metrics pipeline; expose tag to alert rules — owner: Priya Menon — due: 2026-03-21
ENG-12759: Create dashboard-only alert tier and automated escalation rule; update PagerDuty integration mapping — owner: Luis Ortega — due: 2026-03-24
Update runbooks with examples and checklist for deciding when to escalate after confirmation window — owner: Reliability Docs — due: 2026-03-22
QA: Simulate short bursts vs sustained burns in staging to validate suppression logic and no missed pages for real regressions — owner: SRE — due: 2026-03-26
retro_notes: Operational trade-off: increasing confirmation window adds detection latency for true incidents; we chose 3 minutes as a balance after reviewing historical breach durations (median true regression duration ~14 minutes) and customer impact windows.
Decision: Keep a fast-path for opt-in critical routes (customer-facing API keys marked critical) to page immediately; general population uses confirmation window.
Consideration: Long-term work includes adaptive thresholds based on traffic seasonality and per-customer burn-rate alarms to avoid noisy multi-tenant pages.
We will monitor false-negative risk via synthetic probes and a post-deploy monitoring job that validates SLOs are still being detected within acceptable latency.
